normal.name: BraleBradycneme
normal.text: She's awesome, honestly I remember unlocking Mire on that old childhood flash fan game Godzilla Daikaiju Battle Royale when I played it

normal.name: Pook
normal.text: It had uncapped framerates, additional video settings, etc. That's all that's expected for the D1 port afaik based on what I've read so far. Consoles will get a 60FPS patch (maybe some graphical upgrades?) and they'll port it to PC. Nothing that says "Brand new game your old chars don't count."

normal.name: Winson Tang
normal.text: Imagine a world where your favorite video games came on VHS! The nostalgia of loading a game like a classic movie adds a unique twist to gaming culture. Dive into the creative possibilities and what this retro format could mean for gameplay and storytelling. What are your thoughts?

normal.name: Link
normal.text: //I was completely content with not buying another Nintendo product. I didn't like the price jump, the no game on card, I didn't like the gameplay of BOTW/TOTK, But Ocarina Of Time is so special to me. It's one of the earliest games I remember playing. It's so nostalgic to me.

normal.name: Beverley's Horror Corner
normal.text: Having 30 minutes to kill before an eye appointment is a dangerous game. Ended up in my favorite retro shop, and now my collection is three "classics" richer: ​Loch Ness Terror, The Seventh Curse, Vampire Killer Barbys. Worth every penny of that pre-appointment stroll! #PhysicalMedia #CultCinema
normal.media: image: Dvd of Loch Ness Terror and Vampire Killer Barbys and Blu-Ray of The Seventh Curse.

normal.name: Jack Dalrymple 🧩 JackTerror.eth
normal.text: Steam builds a six-second microtrailer from your first store-page video, sampling six different points. Check that little loop before launch. Can someone tell what they actually DO in the game? Tiny asset, real first impression. partner.steamgames.com/doc/store/tr...

normal.name: Ben Lesnick
normal.text: If you do not know this story, he created these neat text based adventure games that were run entirely through DOS batch files and he hid them in three different Origin games! Here's Pix's page about them: www.pixsoriginadventures.co.uk/art-ds-batch...
normal.media: link card: Art D’s Batch Adventures

normal.name: Lunatic Lee
normal.text: Data points for video game history researchers. These are ads from the 1986 Black Friday edition (28 Nov 1986) of the [New York] Daily News. First, an Atari "Home Video Entertainment System"? I think they meant "Video Computer System". They're still using an image of a six-switch system!
normal.media: 2 images: Not sure if it's "H Mart Appliances" or "Homart Appliances," because the spot between the H and M is a TV. The small Atari spot is in the middle of the page. / ATARI Home Video Entertainment System $39 Atari Games $1.99

normal.name: Chris Hazeldine
normal.text: Hear about Queen's Domain. Download the demo. "Wow this game looks incredible!" Die to a giant cricket and a flower that shoots lasers in the first dungeon. God, I remember when I was good at video games. Top 10 in Wipeout Fusion time trials. Yoshimitsu main. Trophies. Now, defeated by a cricket.

normal.name: alice
normal.text: is it not the circumstances of a game in its original context that makes it interesting in the first place? all its idiosyncrasies, the way it looks and sounds, these are all important aspects of a work that are informed by the time & environment it was made in. i really love that about video games!

normal.name: Iron Seagull 🍂
normal.text: In Sonic Racing Crossworlds, you can play as Spongebob while driving a SEGA Genesis with the 32x and the Sonic & Knuckles lock on. Wait, what? Yeah, I love this game.

normal.name: Nick Dymond
normal.text: The Chaos Engine has an adaptive music system but you can hear it skip at the 'exit opened' notification. It was always seamless on the Amiga (mod files) so I assume it's a SNES port issue? Richard Joseph OST goes hard. Bitmap's use of underground music a precursor to other UK games like Wipeout.
normal.media: quotes @timeproof.games: The Chaos Engine / Soldiers of Fortune (SNES, The Bitmap Brothers, 1993)

heated.name: Sean Ehrlich
heated.text: Ugh. Analysis of turnout differential has already begun. This is my cure to log off for many hours. My Election Day routine since Trump first won is to buy a new video game and play it all evening before checking results at 11 or so to avoid the stress. Time to go to the Nintendo eShop.
